## 1. THE PARENT CATEGORY — bubble tea, Taichung, 1986–1988

Bubble tea (珍珠奶茶 zhēnzhū nǎichá) was invented in Taiwan in the mid-to-late 1980s. There are two rival claims and the courts never settled which is true — that fact is itself useful for the deck, because it establishes that the category's founding myth is contested and therefore ownable by whoever tells it best.

**Claim A — Chun Shui Tang (春水堂), Taichung.** Founded 1983 by Liu Han-Chieh (劉漢介), who had returned from Japan where he saw coffee served cold, and began shaking Taiwanese tea over ice — 泡沫紅茶, "foam black tea." The foam is where the word "bubble" actually comes from; it never referred to the pearls. In 1988 (some accounts say 1987), Chun Shui Tang's product-development manager **Lin Hsiu Hui (林秀慧)** tipped her personal afternoon snack — 粉圓 fěnyuán, sweet tapioca balls — into her iced Assam milk tea during a staff meeting. It went on the menu and outsold everything. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, high on the story, medium on the exact year. Verify: Chun Shui Tang corporate history, chunshuitang.com.tw; BBC and CNN Travel have both run long-form versions.]

**Claim B — Hanlin Tea Room (翰林茶館), Tainan.** Founded 1986 by **Tu Tsong-he (涂宗和)**, who says he saw white tapioca balls in Tainan's Ah-bo-liao market (鴨母寮市場), thought they looked like pearls, and made 珍珠茶 with white pearls — switching to the black pearls everyone now knows shortly after. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium-high. Verify: hanlin-tea.com.tw.]

The two companies litigated for roughly a decade. Because no one had patented the drink, the Taiwanese courts declined to award invention to either — the case effectively confirmed the drink belongs to the public domain. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium. Verify: Taiwan Intellectual Property Court records; widely covered in Taiwanese press ~2009–2019.]

Terminology worth getting right in Arabic copy: 珍珠 (zhēnzhū) = "pearl," the small tapioca ball; 波霸 (bōbà) = the large one, Hong Kong slang; "boba" in English comes from 波霸, not from 珍珠.

## 2. THE ACTUAL PRODUCT — brown sugar + pearls + FRESH MILK, no tea

The critical structural point, and the one most Arab operators get wrong: **the original 黑糖珍珠鮮奶 contains no tea at all.** It is brown sugar syrup, brown-sugar-steeped pearls, and cold fresh milk. Removing the tea is what lets the caramelised sugar dominate — this is a dairy-and-sugar drink wearing a tea-shop's clothes.

**The pre-Tiger-Sugar ancestor: 陳三鼎 (Chen San Ding), Gongguan, Taipei.** A small stall by National Taiwan University famous for 青蛙撞奶 — "the frog jumps into the milk" — brown sugar pearls dropped into cold fresh milk. It drew long student queues for years before Tiger Sugar existed and is widely credited inside Taiwan as the popular origin of the brown-sugar-pearl-in-fresh-milk format. Its original Gongguan shop closed around 2019. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium. Verify: Taiwanese food media, 食尚玩家 / ETtoday archives.]

So the honest lineage for the deck: **Tiger Sugar did not invent brown sugar boba. It invented the way it looks.** That distinction is the whole strategic lesson, and it is the lesson SHABIM should quote directly.

## 3. TIGER SUGAR (老虎堂 黑糖 TigerSugar) — Taichung, 2017

Founded in **Taichung, Taiwan, in 2017**, as a single specialist shop selling essentially one drink. Reported first location: Taichung's Yizhong Street / 一中商圈 student night-market district. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE — Taichung + 2017 medium-high; the specific street medium-low.]

**The invention: 虎紋, the tiger stripe.** Thick brown sugar syrup is painted or swirled down the *inside wall* of a clear cup so it clings and runs in dark vertical streaks. Cold fresh milk is poured in; the syrup does not dissolve immediately. The result is a white cup with black stripes — a tiger. The brand is named after its own garnish. Topped with a salted cream-cheese mousse cap (奶蓋 nǎigài) in the signature build, and handed over deliberately UNSTIRRED, with the instruction to shake it yourself. That instruction is not service theatre; it is the mechanism that turns a customer into a videographer, because the stripes only exist for the thirty seconds before the drink is shaken.

**FOUNDER NAME — NOT RELIABLY RECALLED. Do not print a founder name in the deck without checking.** I do not have a confident recall of the individual founder's name and will not invent one. Concrete verification route: Taiwan MOEA 商工登記公示資料查詢服務 (findbiz.nat.gov.tw), search 老虎堂 — the registry returns the 負責人 (responsible person) and the company incorporation date, which will also pin the 2017 founding to a month. This is a free, five-minute check and should be done before the slide ships.

**The 2018 "hand-stirred brown sugar" scandal — put this on a slide.** In 2018 (reported around September), Taiwanese media and the Taichung City Health Bureau established that Tiger Sugar's brown sugar syrup was not hand-stirred in-store as its marketing implied, but bought in pre-made, with reports of added caramel colouring. The company was penalised and forced to change its advertising claims. It happened at the exact peak of the brand's global expansion. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium. Verify: 台中市政府衛生局 press releases 2018; Apple Daily Taiwan / 聯合報 / ETtoday archives, search 老虎堂 黑糖 手炒.]

The lesson for SHABIM, in one line for the deck: **إِنَّ الحِكَايَةَ المُلْصَقَةَ بِالشَّرَابِ هِيَ قِيمَتُهُ وَخَطَرُهُ فِي آنٍ وَاحِد** — the story attached to the drink is simultaneously its value and its liability. If you claim you cook the syrup, you must actually cook the syrup, on camera, in the shop.

## 4. GLOBAL EXPANSION

By 2019 Tiger Sugar had entered Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Macau, Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Australia, Canada and the United States — reportedly passing 100+ outlets across roughly 15 markets within two years of founding. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, low on the count. Verify: tigersugar.com store locator + Taiwanese business press.]

Singapore's first Tiger Sugar outlet — reportedly Capitol Piazza, late 2018 — is the queue-photo moment most often reproduced: reported waits of one to three hours, per-customer purchase caps, and sold-out signs. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium on venue, medium-low on exact date. Verify: Straits Times, TODAYonline, Mothership.sg and 8days.sg archives, Nov 2018 – Feb 2019.]

## THE VIRAL EXPLOSION, 2018–2019 — country by country, with what is checkable

**A methodological warning to put in the deck's footnotes.** TikTok removed public hashtag view totals from the app around 2023–24 and now shows post counts instead; Instagram has never shown view totals for hashtags, only post counts. So every "#bubbletea has N billion views" figure circulating online is a frozen snapshot from before that change, and is a *hashtag aggregate* — the sum of every video ever tagged, including a decade of unrelated content — not the performance of any single video. Label it as such or an investor who checks will catch you.

### JAPAN — the largest single national explosion (第3次タピオカブーム, 2018–2019)

Japan had already had two tapioca booms (roughly 1992 and around 2008). The third, 2018–2019, was an order of magnitude larger and was driven specifically by the brown-sugar/tiger-stripe generation of Taiwanese brands — Tiger Sugar, The Alley (ジ アレイ), Xing Fu Tang (幸福堂), Gong Cha.

- **「タピる」(tapiru), a coined verb meaning "to go drink tapioca," reached the top ten of the 2019 ユーキャン新語・流行語大賞 (U-Can New Words and Buzzwords Award).** [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium-high. Verify: jiyu.co.jp/singo — the award's official archive, 2019 edition.] This is the single strongest quotable proof of cultural penetration available for this product: **the drink became a verb in the Japanese language.** For an Arabic deck this is a gift — the parallel line writes itself: «حِينَ يَصِيرُ المَشْرُوبُ فِعْلًا فِي اللُّغَة، لَمْ يَعُدْ مَشْرُوبًا» (when a drink becomes a verb in the language, it has stopped being a drink).
- タピる also took a category in the 2019 JC・JK流行語大賞 (the schoolgirl buzzword award). [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium.]
- Harajuku's Takeshita Street reached a density of dozens of tapioca stands within roughly eighteen months, then emptied. A 2020 Japanese business book titled 『タピオカ屋はどこへ消えた?』 ("Where did the tapioca shops go?") exists precisely because the collapse was as spectacular as the boom. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium.]
- **The hardest checkable number in the whole file:** Japanese tapioca/cassava-starch import volume spiked sharply in 2019 and collapsed in 2020. I recall reporting of roughly a four-to-sixfold year-on-year increase in 2019. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, LOW. Verify: 財務省貿易統計 (Japan Ministry of Finance Trade Statistics, customs.go.jp), HS code for tapioca/cassava starch, 2017–2021 series. This is free, public, and definitive — if the deck wants ONE unimpeachable number proving the size of a boba boom, this is the one to pull.]

### SOUTH KOREA — 흑당 (heukdang) boom, 2019

The Korean brown-sugar craze ran roughly Q1–Q3 2019, led by 흑화당 (Heukhwadang), 타이거슈가 (Tiger Sugar Korea, first store reportedly Hongdae, 2019) and 더앨리 (The Alley Korea). Korean press covered both the 흑당 열풍 (brown sugar fever) and, within about twelve months, the mass closures. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium. Verify: 조선일보 / 한국경제 / 매일경제 archives, search 흑당 열풍 2019.] The Korean arc is the cleanest evidence available that a brown-sugar boba boom, unsupported by structure, has a life of roughly **twelve to eighteen months** — which matches the "Curve B" 12–24 month window the sibling agent already derived in 07-viral-analogs.json.

### CHINA — and the single best "hard to copy" case study in the world

Brown sugar boba spread through 鹿角巷 (The Alley), 一点点, 喜茶 HEYTEA and 奈雪的茶. The Alley's experience is the one to put on a slide:

**The Alley went viral on a visual it could not legally defend. Reporting around 2019 put its legitimate mainland China estate at roughly 160 stores against something on the order of 7,000 counterfeit outlets** — knock-offs using its name, its deer-head logo and its cup design, because its trademark registration in China had been delayed. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium on the ~7,000 figure; the phenomenon itself is high confidence. Verify: 36Kr, 界面新闻, 第一财经 archives 2019, search 鹿角巷 山寨.] Tiger Sugar suffered the same problem.

**Deck line:** «الشَّكْلُ لا يُحْمَى. النَّمِرُ الَّذِي اخْتَرَعَ خُطُوطَهُ وَجَدَ سَبْعَةَ آلَافِ نَمِرٍ مُزَيَّفٍ يَحْمِلُونَ خُطُوطَه» — the look cannot be protected; the tiger that invented its stripes found seven thousand counterfeit tigers wearing them.

### SINGAPORE — the queue photos, and the emotional-attachment proof

The Tiger Sugar Capitol Piazza opening (reportedly late 2018) produced the multi-hour queue photographs that circulated globally. But the better Singapore data point came later: when Singapore's COVID "circuit breaker" ordered standalone beverage shops shut in **April 2020**, the country produced nationwide, heavily photographed last-day bubble tea queues. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium-high — very widely covered. Verify: Straits Times / CNA, ~21 April 2020.] A category people queue for on the last legal day is a category with genuine emotional attachment, not merely novelty traffic.

### UNITED STATES — the 2021 boba shortage

In spring 2021 (around April), US boba shops rationed and ran out of tapioca pearls because container shipments from Asia were stuck at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. It was covered nationally and #bobashortage trended. [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium-high. Verify: NYT, NPR, LA Times, April 2021; Boba Guys' own public statements.] This is the concrete, dated proof that **the pearl is a supply-chain chokepoint, not a commodity** — the single most important operational argument in this whole brief for a Baghdad operator.

### HASHTAG AGGREGATES — all ESTIMATE, all must be re-pulled live

I could not access any platform this session. The figures below are recalled magnitudes only, given so the parent agent knows what order of number to expect when it pulls them, and each must be re-checked and dated before use:
- Instagram **#bubbletea** — on the order of 5–6 million posts (ESTIMATE, derived from recalled 2023–24 snapshots)
- Instagram **#boba** — on the order of 4 million posts (ESTIMATE)
- Instagram **#brownsugarboba** — on the order of 150,000–300,000 posts (ESTIMATE)
- TikTok **#bubbletea** — on the order of 10–20 billion cumulative views at the last public snapshot before TikTok hid hashtag view totals (ESTIMATE, hashtag aggregate, NOT a single video)
- TikTok **#boba** — on the order of 5–10 billion cumulative views, same caveat (ESTIMATE)

**I deliberately did not fabricate a named single viral video with a view count.** I do not have one I can recall with a creator handle, a date and a number that I would stand behind, and inventing one would be worse than leaving the gap. The verifiable "N million views on DATE by NAMED ACCOUNT" beat that this section needs is best sourced instead from the Japanese customs import data and the 流行語大賞 award — both of which are public, dated, official, and far harder for a sceptical investor to dismiss than a screenshot of a view counter.

## WHY THIS IS STRUCTURALLY HARD TO COPY — and where it is trivially easy

Be honest with the investor about both halves, because half of this product is indefensible and pretending otherwise is what killed The Alley.

### WHAT IS EASY TO COPY (admit this first — it buys credibility for the rest)

**The look.** The tiger stripe is a three-second hand movement on a clear cup. It is not patentable, not trademarkable as a trade dress in most of MENA, and photographs so well that a competitor learns it from your own marketing. The Alley proved the ceiling: roughly 160 legitimate mainland Chinese stores against something on the order of 7,000 counterfeits, all stealing the same deer logo and the same striped cup [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium]. Tiger Sugar was cloned the same way. **Assume that within ninety days of a successful Baghdad launch, striped cups appear on Karrada and in Erbil.** Price that into the plan.

### WHAT IS GENUINELY HARD — four real barriers, in ascending order of strength

**1. The pearl is a perishable, living product with a four-hour clock.**
Tapioca pearls require a 25–40 minute boil, a 20–30 minute steep in hot brown sugar syrup, and are then usable for roughly four hours before starch retrogradation turns them hard, grainy and hollow. They cannot be refrigerated — chilling accelerates the failure. There is no shelf-stable shortcut that tastes right. Every copycat uses five-minute "instant" pearls, and every customer can tell: the QQ is gone, the resistance is gone, and what is left is a cold gummy bead. This is why bubble tea has a persistent quality floor that mediocre operators fall through. It is a labour-discipline moat, and labour discipline is exactly what a franchise SOP system is for.

**2. The pearl is a single-point import chokepoint, and this is documented.**
Cassava is grown in Thailand and Vietnam; the pearl is processed in Taiwan and China; nothing about that chain touches Iraq. The spring 2021 US boba shortage — containers stranded at Los Angeles and Long Beach, shops rationing, #bobashortage trending [MODEL-KNOWLEDGE, medium] — is the dated proof that this input fails under stress. **For SHABIM this cuts both ways and the deck should say so:** dried pearls have a 12–18 month shelf life, so they are importable into Iraq and stockpilable, which means whoever secures the supply line and the buffer inventory FIRST holds a real advantage over a copycat who is buying two boxes at a time from a Baghdad wholesaler. The moat is not the recipe. **The moat is a warehouse.**

**3. The frozen cup is a genuine technical barrier, not a gimmick — and it is SHABIM's actual defensible ground.**
Three separate physics problems have to be solved together, and each one filters out an imitator:

- *Sweetness inverts under cold.* Sweet-taste receptor response falls steeply at low temperature (the TRPM5 mechanism). A frozen presentation of the same syrup tastes flat and thin. The formula must be re-balanced upward for cold — which means the copycat who simply chills your recipe produces a worse drink and blames the concept.
- *The syrup must stay paintable at freezer temperature.* Brown sugar syrup at roughly 65–70 Brix has a freezing point far below −18°C, so it stays viscous and paintable straight from the freezer, and — crucially — the stripe holds SHARPER and bleeds slower against a frozen cup wall than against a room-temperature one. This is the one place where the frozen format makes the signature visual BETTER rather than worse. That is the product insight to build the slide around.
- *The pearls must never be frozen.* Freezing destroys the QQ irreversibly. Therefore the frozen cup must be a **frozen VESSEL with warm pearls dropped in at the moment of service** — not a frozen drink. That two-temperature construction is the actual eating experience: warm elastic pearls in the heart of a frozen cup, «مَطَّاطِيَّةٌ دَافِئَةٌ فِي قَلْبِ البُرُودَة». It is also, conveniently, extremely hard to reverse-engineer from a photograph.

**4. In Baghdad specifically, cold itself is the moat — and this is already session-verified on disk.**
Baghdad runs on 8–12 hours a day of grid power at best [SESSION-VERIFIED, Middle East Monitor Aug 2026, via 07-viral-analogs.json]. A frozen-vessel format requires a freezer that never loses temperature, which requires generator capacity, insulation, and a thermal-mass design — capital and engineering, not a recipe. A street copycat with a striped cup cannot hold −18°C through a July afternoon load-shedding cycle in a city that hits 45°C average highs in July and August and has recorded 51.8°C [SESSION-VERIFIED, 02-iraq-baghdad-market.json]. **The competitor can steal the stripe. He cannot steal the cold.** That is the single strongest sentence available for this section: «يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَسْرِقَ الخَطّ. لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَسْرِقَ البَرْد.»

### AND THE WHITESPACE THAT MAKES IT WORTH DOING

On the sibling agent's session-verified map of every named international operator in Iraq — Cinnabon (Al-Jadriya, Feb 2023), Morelli's Gelato (Jadriya, 2021), Hardee's, Papa John's, Texas Chicken, Burger King, Kyan Café (Basra), Half Million (Iraq Mall, Baghdad) — **not one bubble tea chain appears.** Gong Cha, Chatime and Sharetea are across the GCC; none has crossed into Iraq. Iraq's entire organised branded-beverage estate is 85 outlets [World Coffee Portal, Project Café Middle East 2025 — SESSION-VERIFIED], against 5,130 in Saudi Arabia. **Caveat the deck must carry:** that map was built for coffee, so it proves no bubble tea CHAIN, not zero boba in the city. A one-day field check of Karrada, Mansour, Jadriya and Erbil for independent boba cafés should be done before the word "zero" goes on a slide.

### THE SEVEN-YEAR LESSON, FOR THE CLOSING LINE

One shop opened in Taichung in 2017 selling one striped drink. Within two years it was queued around the block in Singapore, it had turned into a verb in Japanese, and it had spawned seven thousand counterfeits in China. Within eight years the category's leaders were ringing the bell on NASDAQ and the Hong Kong exchange, and its largest chain had more outlets than McDonald's. **The ones who won were never the ones with the best stripe. They were the ones who owned the pearl, the syrup and the cold before anyone else thought to.**
